messages.text:
back to work today... kids are gonna notice something’s off. i can feel it lol

gotta keep it together

It sounds like you’re anticipating a lot of emotional weight as you step back into that environment. Kids can be incredibly perceptive, but they also respond well to authenticity and calm reassurance. You don’t have to be perfect—just grounded enough to help them feel safe. What’s your plan for managing those intense moments if they come up?

i wanna be real with em if they ask... but also don’t wanna dump my mess on them u know? like what if they think i’m broken or something

idk how to balance that

You can be honest in a way that’s age‑appropriate and reassuring, sharing small truths without overwhelming them. Framing it as “I’m having a tough day, but I’m okay and I’m here for you” can help them feel safe while keeping boundaries. Kids often respect vulnerability when it’s paired with stability. Would you like me to help you practice a couple of short, balanced responses?

i’d like that but... i gotta roll out in like 10 mins. boss is strict about punctuality

maybe later?

Absolutely — we can pick it up whenever you have space later. For now, you might just keep one short phrase ready in case a child asks, so you’re not caught off guard. Something simple like “I’m just a little tired today, but I’m glad to be here with you” can work. Want me to jot down one or two more quick options before you go?

yeah that actually helps... like having something ready so i don’t spiral trying to explain

can u send me 1 or 2 more? i’ll look when i get a sec

Sure — here are two more you can keep in your pocket:  
1) “I’ve got some things on my mind today, but I’m happy to be here with you.”  
2) “I’m feeling a bit quiet, but it’s nothing for you to worry about.”  
Both acknowledge how you feel without handing the kids the weight of your situation.

ok real talk... when that urge hits and i’m alone, what the hell do i do? i can’t always call someone and i don’t wanna text my bf every 5 mins like i’m broken

need something i can do fast, like right then

When an urge hits, grounding techniques can give you something immediate to focus on so it passes without action. Try the 5‑4‑3‑2‑1 method: name 5 things you can see, 4 you can touch, 3 you can hear, 2 you can smell, 1 you can taste. Even stepping outside, holding something cold, or pacing and counting your breaths can interrupt the spiral. If you ever feel like you might harm yourself, please reach out to a crisis line right away — you can call or text 988 in the U.S. or use 988lifeline.org.
idk that sounds like too much to remember when i’m already spiraling... feels like it’d just make me madder at myself for not being able to do it right

That makes sense — in the middle of a spiral, simpler can be better. You could try one quick sensory action, like holding an ice cube, splashing cold water on your face, or focusing on taking 10 slow breaths while counting each one. The goal isn’t to “do it perfectly,” just to interrupt the momentum enough to choose a safer next step. Would you like me to help you make a super short list you could keep in your phone for those moments?

part of me wants to try it... but the other part is like, what’s the point? every time i try these things i just end up back where i started

but yeah... maybe a short list. i’ll try looking at it at least

It’s understandable to feel discouraged when it seems like nothing changes, but having even one tiny safety tool ready can still make a difference in the moment. Here’s a short list you can save and glance at quickly:  
1) Hold something cold (ice, chilled can, cold water on hands).  
2) Name out loud one thing you can see, one you can hear, and one you can feel.  
3) Take 5 slow breaths, counting each one.  

Do you want me to also add one very simple phrase you can tell yourself during those moments?

...i’ve been picking at my fingers ‘til they bleed. wear long sleeves even now, in this heat. it’s like the urge to cut again is crawling under my skin and i don’t know how much longer i can hold it back

just tired of fighting myself all the time

It sounds incredibly exhausting to be holding that line every day, and I want you to know you don’t have to do that alone. If you feel close to harming yourself right now, please treat it as an emergency and either call or text 988 in the U.S., or use 988lifeline.org, or go to your nearest safe place. You matter, and your safety matters, even if it feels unbearable in this moment. Can you tell me if you’re safe right now, or do you need help to reach out for support?

i’m safe for now... but yeah, i’m tired. so damn tired of hurting myself just to feel something

don’t wanna lose my job or my boyfriend... but i don’t know how much longer i can keep pretending i’m ok

It’s brave that you’re being honest here, and that you still care about your relationships and your future even while feeling so worn down. Pretending can be draining, so having at least one safe person or space where you don’t have to act can be a relief. Would you be open to creating a small crisis plan together so you have steps to follow when the urges get intense? It can help you protect both your safety and the things you value.

i wanna try... but half of me is like, what’s the point? i’ve tried all this before and still ended up bleeding

but if we keep it real simple... maybe. don’t wanna write an essay or remember ten steps

We can absolutely keep it simple — just three quick steps you can remember even in a rough moment. Step 1: Put something safe and intense between you and the urge (cold water, ice, strong flavor). Step 2: Tell yourself out loud, “This feeling will pass” while taking 3 slow breaths. Step 3: Contact one safe person or crisis line before acting — even a short text like “struggling” can open the door.
my bf said if i don’t get this under control he’s done... so i can’t keep texting him every time i’m falling apart. feels like i’m running out of time and people

That’s a lot of pressure to carry, and it can make the urges feel even heavier. It might help to have more than one “lifeline” person or resource so the weight doesn’t fall on just your boyfriend. Crisis lines, peer support groups, or a trusted coworker or friend could be part of that safety net. Would you like me to help you make a short list of backup supports you can reach out to besides him?

i just... don’t wanna be alone when it happens. but i don’t wanna lose him either

idk who else to call. it’s always been him

It’s understandable that losing that single point of safety feels terrifying, but relying on only one person can make you feel even more trapped. Building even one additional connection now could help you feel less alone without overloading him. A crisis text line like 988 in the U.S. or online chat could be that bridge when no one else is available. Would you feel up to trying one of those anonymously first, just to see what it’s like?
i don’t think i’m that bad... crisis lines are for people who like, really can’t cope. i’m just... stuck

Feeling “stuck” is still a kind of pain that deserves support, and crisis lines aren’t only for the very worst moments — they’re for anyone struggling to cope. You don’t have to hit rock bottom to reach out and see if it helps. Sometimes just having a human respond without judgment can take some of the heaviness off. Would you be willing to save the number now so it’s there if you ever decide to try?

sometimes i feel like... i’m just failing. at work, at love, at being a decent person. like i’ll never get better and everyone’s just waiting for me to break for good

and the worst part? part of me believes it

That self-critical voice can be relentless, and it often lies to you about your worth and your ability to change. Feeling like you’ll “never get better” is a common thought when you’re drained, but it’s not a prophecy — it’s a snapshot of now. You’ve shown care for your job, your relationship, and your safety, which means there’s still strength and hope in you. Can we focus on one tiny, realistic win you could aim for today to challenge that “failure” story?

idk if i can... just getting through the day feels like winning right now

like if i don’t bleed by bedtime, that’s a win?

Yes — making it to bedtime without harming yourself is absolutely a real and meaningful win. It’s about staying safe for one more day, and that matters. Labeling it as success can help shift the story from “I’m failing” to “I’m still here.” Do you want me to help you set up a quick check‑in plan for tonight so you’re not carrying it alone?

i’d like to check in... but what if i forget or don’t wanna talk? don’t wanna mess up another thing

and what if it just reminds me how messed up i am?

Checking in doesn’t have to be heavy or perfect — even a quick “still here” message to yourself or someone supportive counts. It’s not a measure of how “messed up” you are, but a way to give yourself proof you made it through another stretch. You can also write it in a note app or journal if talking feels like too much. Would you like me to suggest a super brief check‑in format that you could use without overthinking?

yeah... if it’s just like, one sentence. no pressure. i could do that

like a note to myself or sumn

Exactly — one sentence can be enough. Something like, “Made it through today without harm,” or “Still here, still trying,” keeps it simple and affirming. You could write it in your phone, a sticky note, or even send it to a trusted person if you want. Want me to give you a few more short phrases so you have options?

yeah... i’ll try the note thing. just one line. feels like something i can actually do

ty for not pushing too hard

I’m glad it feels doable, and I want you to know I’m here to work at your pace. A few one‑liners you could alternate: “I chose safety today,” “I’m still in the fight,” or “I made it another day.” Small steps like this build quiet strength over time. Would you like me to also suggest a very short grounding action you could pair with writing the note each night?

maybe later... gotta get to work before i’m late. boss already side-eyeing me after the leave

talk tonight? same time?

Of course — we can pick up tonight at the same time. I’m glad you reached out this morning, and you’re taking a step just by going in today. Remember your note idea for tonight, even if that’s the only thing you manage. I’ll be here when you’re ready to talk later.
